prompt: Design a vacation rental booking app like Airbnb — browse beautiful stays by destination, filter by price and rating, and open a listing to see photos, amenities, guest reviews, and book your stay. Make it feel warm, trustworthy, and modern.
title: StayFinder

issues.description: The visible SCENES SVG contains a linearGradient. Gradients are prohibited by the universal design law unless explicitly permitted by the company language, and Airbnb's brief does not permit them.
The visible SCENES SVG contains a linearGradient, violating the no-gradient rule. Replace it with token-based flat artwork or photographic media.

The visible listing imagery is stylized generated scene art rather than photo-first rental photography. This weakens Airbnb's signature visual language and the brief's requirement for real-looking listing photos.
The visible detail imagery uses the same stylized scene treatment instead of a convincing 4–5 image gallery for one real-looking stay.

The expandable summary is implemented as a div with role=button. It has keyboard handling but no visible focus ring or aria-expanded state, violating the interactive-element accessibility requirement.
The component references --card-foreground, which is not among the approved tokens shown in the design language. Use --foreground or another defined token.
The compact policy variant uses undefined --color-secondary, --color-muted, --color-primary, and --color-foreground variables instead of the approved token names.
The shared Card component hardcodes rounded-xl instead of using the theme radius scale. This undermines consistent radius and token discipline wherever the component is rendered.
Both screens use the generic Get started / Learn more CTA pair from the copy data. The booking product needs specific actions such as Search stays on home and Reserve on detail.

The home screen must have one dominant browse moment. Any rendered chart, metric band, or extra custom card module alongside the photo catalog would create competing dominant moments and violate the two-screen home contract.

The detail screen must be scoped to one stay only. Any rendered catalog, search, stats, chart, or unrelated activity content must be removed; the page should follow gallery → one booking summary card → fact rows → reviews → trust band.
The listing grid uses colorful vector illustrations instead of the brief's photo-first, human, trust-building rental imagery. This is a major mismatch with the Airbnb-inspired reference language.
The gallery is made from repeated crops of a generic illustration rather than a convincing 4–5 image gallery of one real stay. It does not create the expected photo-led booking experience.
Large blank areas and duplicated StayFinder/footer blocks below the review list make the page look broken or partially rendered.
The screen omits most required detail information: amenities, sleeping arrangements, house rules, cancellation policy, and meaningful host response/review trust signals.
The oversized 'Find an affordable stay' headline and substantial whitespace make the screen read more like a marketing landing page than a browse/catalog home screen.

The desktop grid is a three-column set of uniform cards rather than the brief's comfortable single-column mobile-first catalog. The mobile behavior is not demonstrated and should be verified at 375px.
The dominant gallery is followed by a sparse summary/details area with excessive vertical separation, weakening hierarchy and the intended gallery → summary → facts → reviews sequence.

The copy is mostly generic product scaffolding such as 'Full info page for one item' and 'Mobile vacation rental booking app' rather than warm, specific stay, neighborhood, host, and cancellation language.
The header and search controls feel closer to a generic dashboard than the warm Airbnb-style search hero with rounded, photo-led marketplace navigation.

reviewResult.summary: The implementation compiles and has several useful rental-specific components, including search summaries, amenities, policies, and host trust signals. However, it currently conflicts with the brand's photo-first direction, uses prohibited gradients and undefined token names, has an accessibility defect in the expandable search summary, and requires strict enforcement of the two-screen composition and single-item detail contract. The generic CTA copy also needs to be replaced with booking-specific language.
requiredFixes: Replace the inline SVG linear gradients in src/screens/home.jsx and src/screens/detail.jsx with flat token-based fills or shipped rental photography; gradients are prohibited by the universal design law.

Use real-looking rental photography from the shipped references or equivalent photo assets in src/screens/home.jsx and src/screens/detail.jsx. The visible scene artwork does not meet the Airbnb photo-first, human-touch direction.
Convert the interactive summary container in src/components/StaySearchSummary.jsx from a clickable div into a real button or add a visible focus ring, aria-expanded, and complete keyboard behavior.

Replace undefined color variables such as --card-foreground and --color-secondary/--color-muted/--color-primary/--color-foreground in src/components/HostTrustProfile.jsx and src/components/StayPolicies.jsx with the approved theme tokens.
Update src/data.js so the home action is a specific browse/search action and the detail action is Reserve; remove the generic Get started / Learn more CTA pair.

Ensure src/screens/home.jsx contains only the search toolbar, catalog grid, and one dominant browse moment; remove any rendered generic chart, stats, or custom card modules that compete with the photo-led catalog.

Ensure src/screens/detail.jsx renders only the selected stay's gallery, one booking summary card, fact rows, amenity/policy rows, reviews, and one quiet trust band; remove any catalog, search, stats, or chart content.
Replace the fixed rounded-xl surface in src/components/Card.jsx with the theme radius token so card geometry follows the shared radius scale.
home: Replace the flat illustrated listing artwork with real-looking, photo-first rental photography for every stay card, while preserving the heart/save control and readable listing metadata.
detail: Replace the repeated illustrated gallery tiles with 4–5 distinct photographs of the same property, using a photo mosaic with consistent aspect ratios.
detail: Remove the large empty and duplicate footer/loading-like sections below the reviews and tighten the vertical rhythm so the page feels complete rather than unfinished.
detail: Add the required single-item facts and trust content: amenities, sleeping arrangements, house rules, cancellation policy, host response time, review count, and verified/Superhost status.
home: Reduce the marketing-landing-page feel by making the search toolbar and catalog the clear primary story; use a more compact browse header and avoid the oversized generic headline.

home: Ensure the mobile layout becomes a comfortable single-column listing feed at 375px, with the search context, price/rating selectors, and active criteria remaining visible without cramped controls.

detail: Make the booking summary card show nightly price, selected dates, guest count, estimated total, cancellation terms, and one clearly dominant coral Reserve action; keep secondary Save action quieter.
